neutral_facts.value: The accused individuals were alleged to have duped a complainant by taking Rs. 30 lakhs under the pretense of sending his son to America for a permanent job. The complainant paid the amount in several instalments, but the accused failed to fulfill the promise and issued a cheque for Rs. 30 lakhs which was dishonoured due to insufficient funds. The complainant filed a First Information Report (FIR) under Section 420 of the Indian Penal Code. The accused applied for anticipatory bail, which was denied by the trial court and the High Court. The accused challenged the denial of anticipatory bail, arguing that the case should be tried by the Gram Panchayat under the Punjab Panchayati Raj Act. The Supreme Court dismissed the appeals, holding that the investigation should be conducted by the police and the case should be tried by the regular criminal court due to the serious nature of the allegations.

legal_principle_applied.value: The Supreme Court applied the principle that the jurisdiction conferred on the Gram Panchayat cannot take away the power of the police. The police cannot be abridged or taken away under any circumstances, and the Gram Panchayat has no jurisdiction until the stage of completion of investigation.
